payload.description: An AI Assistant that’s easy to setup, does your work 24/7, knows your preferences and gets better over time.

payload.text:
A personal AI assistant that evolves with you.
It learns how you work, remembers what matters, and acts before you ask. Yours to name, shape, and extend.

--- ## What it does | Area | Summary | | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Memory** | **Learns what matters and forgets what doesn't.** Structured memory items — identity, preferences, projects, events — extracted with source attribution and deduplication. Hybrid retrieval (dense + sparse) ranks results semantically and lexically, with staleness windows per memory type. Per-user and per-channel isolation. Embeddings run locally by default. | | **Identity** | **Becomes its own.** Behavior lives in SOUL.md, and during onboarding the assistant observes how you communicate and writes its own personality files. A per-user journal captures its reflections on past interactions. NOW.md acts as an ephemeral scratchpad for current focus and active threads. | | **Proactivity** | **Reaches out when something matters, without being asked.** Every hour it checks in with itself: re-reads its notes, notices what's unfinished or due soon, and sends a message if needed. Notifications are routed to the right channel and won't interrupt you if you're already talking. | | **Security** | **Fail-closed by design.** Actor identity is resolved once (guardian, trusted, or unknown) and enforced everywhere. Untrusted actors cannot read or write memory, trigger tools, or escalate. Credentials live in a separate process and never reach the model. Every tool runs in a sandbox. |

--- ## Get started **1. [Download the latest release](https://vellum.ai/download)** **2. Open the app and pick your mode** - **Managed** — sign in via Vellum Cloud, no local runtime required - **Local** — everything runs on your machine **3. Hatch your assistant** - Give it a name, a personality, and the keys to your work Prefer the terminal? See CLI install below. --- ## Quick demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/009bd0ae-95ac-4cf3-81bc-d54cd8631583 --- ## CLI
Install and common commands
The CLI works but the desktop app is our primary focus. Available for advanced users, contributors, and non-macOS environments. **Install** ```bash bun install -g vellum vellum hatch ``` **Install from source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant.git cd vellum-assistant ./setup.sh source ~/.bashrc vellum hatch ``` **Common commands** ```bash vellum wake # start services vellum sleep # stop services, keep data vellum client # interact through the terminal vellum ps # view running assistants vellum terminal # open a shell into a managed assistant container vellum upgrade # upgrade to latest version ``` All commands target the default assistant. If you have multiple, pass the assistant ID as the second argument.
--- ## Infra and security | Area | Summary | | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Trust engine** | **Decides who can do what, and defaults to no.** Fail-closed trust system that resolves actor identity once (guardian, trusted, or unknown) and enforces it everywhere. Untrusted actors cannot read or write memory, trigger tools, or escalate. Your credentials live in a separate process and never reach the model. | | **Skills** | **Add new capabilities through sandboxed plugins.** Manifest-driven plugins (SKILL.md + TOOLS.json) that inject tools and prompt sections at runtime. Skills can be bundled, installed from a catalog, or added from the workspace. | | **Channels** | **One assistant, everywhere you need it.** Use it from the macOS app, Telegram, or Slack, with shared memory across all of them. More channels coming soon. | | **Multi-provider support** | **Swap models without changing anything else.** Supports Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Ollama for local models. Embeddings follow the same pattern: local ONNX by default, with automatic fallback to cloud providers. | --- ## Foundational documents The canonical sources for who we are and how we talk about what we're building. The docs site at [vellum.ai/docs](https://vellum.ai/docs) is a rendered view of these files. | Doc | What it is | | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Constitution](CONSTITUTION.md) | Who we are, what we believe, and what we refuse to compromise on | | [Glossary](GLOSSARY.md) | The shared vocabulary we use to talk about personal intelligence | --- ## Documentation | Section | What's covered | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [Architecture](https://vellum.ai/docs/developer-guide/architecture) | Platform domains, repo structure, runtime · clients · gateway | | [Security & Permissions](https://vellum.ai/docs/developer-guide/security) | Sandbox, credentials, trust rules, permission modes | | [Features & Capabilities](https://vellum.ai/docs/developer-guide/features) | Integrations, dynamic skills, browser, attachments, media embeds | | [API & Communication](https://vellum.ai/docs/developer-guide/api) | SSE event stream, event payloads, remote access | | [Development Workflow](https://vellum.ai/docs/developer-guide/development-workflow) | Claude Code commands, parallel PRs, review loops, release pipeline | 📖 **[Full documentation →](https://vellum.ai/docs)** --- ## Contributing We welcome contributions from everyone. - **Development**: The [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) will help you get started. - Make sure to check out our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Community - 💬 [Discord](https://vellum.ai/community) - 🐛 [Issues](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/issues) ## License MIT — see [License](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant?tab=MIT-1-ov-file). Integration logos from [Simple Icons](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons), licensed [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Vellum Assistant is open-source software built by [Vellum AI](https://vellum.ai), a for-profit company. We also offer a managed product, the [Vellum Platform](https://vellum.ai/platform), which sustains the business. Free to use and modify under MIT, and we're committed to keeping it that way. ---

Built with 💚 by Vellum

# Contributing

Thank you for your interest in Vellum Assistant! We welcome contributions of all kinds — bug fixes, new features, documentation improvements, and more.

## Before you start

- **Bug reports and feature requests**: [Open an issue](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/issues). Use the provided templates.
- **Security vulnerabilities**: Report these privately. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- **Questions and discussion**: Join us on [Discord](https://vellum.ai/community).

## Development setup

### Getting started

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant.git
cd vellum-assistant
./setup.sh    # installs Bun (if needed), installs deps, links packages, registers the global vellum CLI
```

Verify your setup:

```bash
vellum --version
```

### Running the assistant locally

**macOS app (recommended):**

```bash
./clients/macos/build.sh run   # build + launch + watch for changes (auto-rebuild)
```

**CLI only:**

> **Note:** CLI interaction hasn't been heavily tested — we welcome contributions to improve the experience.

```bash
vellum hatch   # first-time setup (only needed once)
vellum wake    # start an existing assistant
vellum client  # interact with your assistant through the terminal
vellum sleep   # stop but do not remove an existing assistant
```

### Running tests

```bash
# Assistant
cd assistant && bun run test

# CLI
cd cli && bun run test

# Gateway
cd gateway && bun run test
```

### Linting and type checking

```bash
# From any package directory (assistant/, cli/, gateway/)
bun run lint
bun run typecheck
```

### Using AI coding assistants

If you use Claude Code, see [.claude/README.md](.claude/README.md) for setup (shared slash commands, fast mode, typical workflow).

## Project structure

| Directory | What it is |
|---|---|
| `assistant/` | Core assistant runtime — memory, tools, skills, scheduling, integrations |
| `gateway/` | Public ingress — webhooks, API routes, OAuth callbacks |
| `cli/` | The `vellum` CLI |
| `clients/` | Native clients (macOS) and browser extension |
| `apps/` | End-user app surfaces (web, iOS, macOS/Electron, Chrome extension) — scaffold |
| `credential-executor/` | Isolated credential execution service |
| `packages/` | Shared internal packages |
| `skills/` | Skill definitions |

For deeper architectural context, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) and the domain-specific docs linked from it.

## Active migrations

Some directories in this repo are landing zones for in-progress
relocations. They build green but are not the live source for the
corresponding surface yet. Please avoid landing feature work in these
directories until the move is complete.

| Directory | Status |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/` | Active migration target — Vite + React Router v7 SPA for the assistant web app. Code is being incrementally migrated from a separate repo. See [`apps/web/README.md`](apps/web/README.md) for local dev setup, [`apps/web/docs/CONVENTIONS.md`](apps/web/docs/CONVENTIONS.md) and [`apps/web/docs/STATE_MANAGEMENT.md`](apps/web/docs/STATE_MANAGEMENT.md) for architecture and state, and [`apps/web/docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md`](apps/web/docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) for coding style. |
| `apps/chrome-extension/` | Move in progress from [`clients/chrome-extension/`](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/tree/main/clients/chrome-extension). |

## Submitting a pull request

1. Fork the repo and create a branch from `main`.
2. Make your changes. Write tests where applicable.
3. Make sure CI passes locally: `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test` in the relevant package(s).
4. Open a PR against `main`. Fill out the PR template.
5. A maintainer will review your PR. We aim to respond within a few business days.

### PR guidelines

- **Keep PRs focused.** One logical change per PR. Smaller PRs get reviewed faster.
- **PR titles** follow conventional commits format: `type(scope): description` (e.g., `feat(slack): add user token support`, `fix(cli): handle missing config`).
- **We assume AI was used.** That's fine — just include the prompt or plan you used in the PR description.
- **Don't submit PRs against `release/*` branches.** These are for release management only.

### What makes a good contribution

- Fixes a bug you encountered while using the assistant
- Improves documentation or developer experience
- Adds test coverage for untested paths
- Implements a feature you've discussed in an issue or on Discord

## Code of Conduct

All participants are expected to follow our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## License

By contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

Closing in favor of an egress-jail-based cost recorder. Vargas pointed out (correctly) that synthesizing `usage` events from `usage_progress` only works for the Vellum daemon harness — every other benchmark harness needs its own translation layer.

The egress jail already sees every LLM HTTP request/response on the way out, regardless of which provider client (or which evals harness) made the call. Recording usage/cost there means a single source of truth across all harnesses with no per-harness shim.

Will draft the spec for the egress-jail-based recorder before writing code so we agree on the shape first.

payload.author: vellum-apollo-bot
payload.body:
Closing — this was the wrong abstraction layer.

The right place to capture LLM usage is the egress jail (`evals/src/lib/egress/`), which is already wired into the runner generically (`agent.readUsageRecords?.()` at `run-once.ts:325`) and is already invoked on every vellum-* run via `applyDockerEgressJail` in the vellum adapter. Doing it at the jail boundary captures real wire-level usage for **every** harness (vellum, hermes, future adapters) instead of needing per-adapter shape translation.

The Tier B run's `egress-usage.ndjson` was created but empty — that's the actual bug to chase. Followup: investigate why the mitmproxy sidecar did not intercept the assistant container's Anthropic calls on the AWS sandbox.

payload.body:
<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure</summary>

# Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure

## Overview

Make the memory-v3 topic tree **self-maintaining** so it stays coherent as the
corpus grows and reorganizes over weeks/months, without a human babysitting a
batch script. The maintainer (the assistant) keeps her own structure current as
a natural extension of how she already consolidates memory; deterministic
plumbing keeps referential integrity; a green-suppressed health report surfaces
the cases automation can't resolve.

Four capabilities, mirroring how v2 consolidation already works (an assistant
turn for judgment + a mechanical follow-up for indexing):

1. **Assignment stays current** — page→leaf assignment lives in page frontmatter
   (`leaves:`), exactly like v2's `edges:`. The maintainer sets it as she files a
   page; a post-consolidation classifier **unions in** anything she missed; the
   needle index rebuilds. Drift becomes structurally hard.
2. **Health report** — at the consolidation trigger, a flag-gated block reports
   coverage gaps, pipeline failures, and judgment-only candidates (new leaves,
   stale labels). Shown only when something is actionable.
3. **Tree gardening** — the maintainer can restructure the tree (add / rename /
   move / split / merge / delete leaves). A deterministic reconciler keeps all
   references intact, re-homes pages so none are orphaned, and snapshots for
   rollback. Stable leaf `id`s make reorg cheap and safe to repeat.
4. **Core editing** — the maintainer owns the always-on `core.json` set, with
   validation and an always-on page-count/cost preview.

## Design rationale (the "why")

- **Why frontmatter, not `assignments.json`:** v2 already stores structural links
  (`edges:`) in page frontmatter as the single source of truth — no side table.
  Mirroring that makes assignment *born with the page and maintained with it*, so
  it can't silently drift. `assignments.json` becomes a derived/fallback export,
  not the source.
- **Why union (maintainer ∪ classifier):** the maintainer read the source
  material and has context a summary-only classifier lacks (cross-domain links,
  nuance); the classifier systematically sweeps all leaves and catches the
  obvious homes she skips mid-consolidation. Unioning their picks yields strictly
  higher recall than either alone, consistent with the multi-home design. Cost:
  multi-home creeps from ~3.2 toward ~4–5 leaves/page — acceptable; L2 + the
  working-set cap absorb it.
- **Why a health report even with auto-classify:** automation can fail silently
  (a classifier follow-up errors → pages stay unrouted). The report is the
  visible heartbeat that catches failures and surfaces judgment-only cases
  (new-leaf candidates, label staleness) that automation deliberately won't touch.
- **Why stable leaf `id`s:** the system is meant to be reorganized repeatedly.
  Keying assignments on leaf *paths* makes every rename a fragile mass-rewrite.
  An immutable `id` per leaf (path = location only) lets the reconciler diff trees
  by id — unambiguous rename/split/merge/delete detection — so reorg is cheap and
  safe to repeat. Page frontmatter keeps using readable *paths*; the reconciler
  uses id-continuity to migrate those paths.
- **Why not fold all of this into the bundled consolidation prompt:** the
  maintainer runs a *custom* consolidation prompt via
  `config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`. The assignment step is added to
  *her* prompt (a workspace file) — zero blast radius on the bundled prompt or
  other installs. Only the loader/index/job changes are code.

## Verified integration points (current code)

- v3 loader: `src/memory/v3/tree.ts` — `resolveDataDir()` (32-36) →
  `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/`; `loadLeafTree(dataDir)` (99-137) builds `byPage`
  from `assignments.json` (`Record<Slug, LeafPath[]>`, line 126).
- Leaf schema: `src/memory/v3/types.ts:14-17` `LeafFrontmatter { path, in_core }`;
  pa

## Self-review + integrated verification (lead) ✅ — final

3 fresh-eyes passes (faithfulness, integration, slop) → **5 gaps found & fixed** (#32717–#32721): de-dup'd the `memory_v3_maintain` consolidation enqueue (was 2×, broke its own test), registered the orphaned leaf-id migration (renumbered 093), pointed CLI `health`/`set-core` at the authoritative `leaves:` frontmatter, made `reconcile` help honest, and wired the maintenance interval backstop.

### Verification result
- **`bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean** (fully-installed worktree).
- **All 18 `src/memory/v3/` test files + the 3 touched non-v3 files pass in isolation:** consolidation-job 21/0, backfill-leaf-ids 6/0, memory-v3 CLI 7/0, jobs-worker-v2-schedule 15/0, tree 10/0, maintain-job 7/0, router (isolated) green, shadow-plugin (isolated) green, live-integration 4/0, etc.
- **Full `src/memory/v3/` directory sweep is RED (≈19 fail) due to a test-harness mock leak, not product code.**

### Why the sweep is red (diagnosed, not product defects)
1. bun runs `live-integration.test.ts` first; in a worktree where `packages/service-contracts` wasn't `bun install`-ed, it throws `Cannot find module '@vellumai/service-contracts/credential-rpc'` as an **unhandled error between tests**, aborting that file mid-run.
2. Because it aborts, its process-global `mock.module("../../../providers/provider-send-message.js")` is **never torn down** and **leaks into every subsequent file** in the same bun process — so `router`, `shadow-plugin`, `tree`, `maintain-job` see the real provider / a stale spy and fail, despite passing standalone. (Counts even drift run-to-run — classic cross-file state bleed.)

Neither cause is a defect in this PR's product code: `credential-rpc` is a normal source export that resolves in a properly-installed checkout, and every file is green alone. **This branch did, however, add new v3 test files using the same un-guarded `mock.module` pattern** that several pre-existing v3 tests (`orchestrate`/`router`/`selector`/`live-integration`, all unchanged here) already use.

### Recommended follow-up (separate PR, test-only)
Make the v3 tests' `mock.module` installs restore-on-teardown (delegate-to-real-unless-flag, per the repo's known bun mock-leak pattern) so `bun test src/memory/v3/` is green under a single-process sweep. payload.body:
<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure</summary>

# Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure

## Overview

Make the memory-v3 topic tree **self-maintaining** so it stays coherent as the
corpus grows and reorganizes over weeks/months, without a human babysitting a
batch script. The maintainer (the assistant) keeps her own structure current as
a natural extension of how she already consolidates memory; deterministic
plumbing keeps referential integrity; a green-suppressed health report surfaces
the cases automation can't resolve.

Four capabilities, mirroring how v2 consolidation already works (an assistant
turn for judgment + a mechanical follow-up for indexing):

1. **Assignment stays current** — page→leaf assignment lives in page frontmatter
   (`leaves:`), exactly like v2's `edges:`. The maintainer sets it as she files a
   page; a post-consolidation classifier **unions in** anything she missed; the
   needle index rebuilds. Drift becomes structurally hard.
2. **Health report** — at the consolidation trigger, a flag-gated block reports
   coverage gaps, pipeline failures, and judgment-only candidates (new leaves,
   stale labels). Shown only when something is actionable.
3. **Tree gardening** — the maintainer can restructure the tree (add / rename /
   move / split / merge / delete leaves). A deterministic reconciler keeps all
   references intact, re-homes pages so none are orphaned, and snapshots for
   rollback. Stable leaf `id`s make reorg cheap and safe to repeat.
4. **Core editing** — the maintainer owns the always-on `core.json` set, with
   validation and an always-on page-count/cost preview.

## Design rationale (the "why")

- **Why frontmatter, not `assignments.json`:** v2 already stores structural links
  (`edges:`) in page frontmatter as the single source of truth — no side table.
  Mirroring that makes assignment *born with the page and maintained with it*, so
  it can't silently drift. `assignments.json` becomes a derived/fallback export,
  not the source.
- **Why union (maintainer ∪ classifier):** the maintainer read the source
  material and has context a summary-only classifier lacks (cross-domain links,
  nuance); the classifier systematically sweeps all leaves and catches the
  obvious homes she skips mid-consolidation. Unioning their picks yields strictly
  higher recall than either alone, consistent with the multi-home design. Cost:
  multi-home creeps from ~3.2 toward ~4–5 leaves/page — acceptable; L2 + the
  working-set cap absorb it.
- **Why a health report even with auto-classify:** automation can fail silently
  (a classifier follow-up errors → pages stay unrouted). The report is the
  visible heartbeat that catches failures and surfaces judgment-only cases
  (new-leaf candidates, label staleness) that automation deliberately won't touch.
- **Why stable leaf `id`s:** the system is meant to be reorganized repeatedly.
  Keying assignments on leaf *paths* makes every rename a fragile mass-rewrite.
  An immutable `id` per leaf (path = location only) lets the reconciler diff trees
  by id — unambiguous rename/split/merge/delete detection — so reorg is cheap and
  safe to repeat. Page frontmatter keeps using readable *paths*; the reconciler
  uses id-continuity to migrate those paths.
- **Why not fold all of this into the bundled consolidation prompt:** the
  maintainer runs a *custom* consolidation prompt via
  `config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`. The assignment step is added to
  *her* prompt (a workspace file) — zero blast radius on the bundled prompt or
  other installs. Only the loader/index/job changes are code.

## Verified integration points (current code)

- v3 loader: `src/memory/v3/tree.ts` — `resolveDataDir()` (32-36) →
  `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/`; `loadLeafTree(dataDir)` (99-137) builds `byPage`
  from `assignments.json` (`Record<Slug, LeafPath[]>`, line 126).
- Leaf schema: `src/memory/v3/types.ts:14-17` `LeafFrontmatter { path, in_core }`;
  pa

payload.body:
## Second pass — addresses Codex P2 + CI Type Check

**Codex feedback addressed** ([comment](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/pull/32677#discussion_r3329067798))

History payloads reference `toolCalls` / `surfaces` *positionally* — the renderer (`resolveToolCall`, `resolveSurface` in `transcript-message-body.tsx`) falls back to `parseInt(id, 10) → array[idx]` when the id matches no real member id. The first pass concatenated `toolCalls` / `surfaces` arrays but left donor `{ type: "tool", id: "0" }` / `{ type: "surface", id: "0" }` entries unchanged, so on the folded long-turn bubble the donor entries resolved to the survivor's `toolCalls[0]` / `surfaces[0]` — wrong progress card / wrong surface at every page boundary.

**Fix:** `remapAdjacentContentOrder` now shifts positional ids for all four kinds (text, attachment, tool/toolCall, surface) by the survivor's corresponding array length. Streaming-shape entries that carry a real id (`toolu_…`, surfaceId UUIDs) bypass the shift via a `/^\d+$/` gate — they resolve via the id-keyed first-pass lookup, so any remap would corrupt them.

**CI Type Check fix:** `DisplayAttachment` requires `previewUrl` — added `previewUrl: null` to the three test fixtures that omitted it.

**Tests:** 3 new cases under `mergeAdjacentAssistantMessages · contentOrder remap`:
- `shifts tool:N positional ids in the donor by survivor.toolCalls.length (history shape)`
- `shifts surface:N positional ids in the donor by survivor.surfaces.length (history shape)`
- `leaves real (non-numeric) toolCall / surface ids untouched (streaming shape)`

Plus the existing `interleaved text + tool positional entries remap each by their own offset` updated to exercise both offsets simultaneously.

**Verification**
- `bun test src/domains/chat/utils/message-merge.test.ts` → 18/18 pass
- All 7 CI checks green on `8259bd8717` ✅

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Live Injection Mode</summary>

# Memory v3 — Live Injection Mode

## Overview

Make memory-v3 an actual injection source (not just shadow telemetry) behind a
new **default-off** `memory-v3-live` feature flag, distinct from
`memory-v3-shadow`. When on for a conversation, the v3 orchestrator's
`finalInjection` becomes the injected `<memory>` block — **suppressing v2's
injection** so there is exactly one memory source — with two supporting
disciplines: (1) the `<memory>` block is stripped from **all** historical user
messages each turn (keeps the context window lean and makes history
byte-stable/cacheable), and (2) the provider call is told the latest user
message is volatile so the prompt-cache anchor lands on the most recent
**stable** message instead of the changing current turn.

**v2 is left completely untouched.** Every change is gated on `memory-v3-live`;
when the flag is off, the v2 injection path, its last-message-only strip, and
its cache-anchor behavior are bit-for-bit identical to today. The flag flip,
A/B, and cutover remain operational follow-ups outside this plan — this plan
ends with live injection fully implemented and primed behind a default-off
flag.

The foundational provider change (PR L1) is a **standalone, v2-safe**
generalization of cache-anchor placement that is independently useful and
mergeable on its own; it does not depend on any other PR here.

## PR L1: Provider cache-anchor flag for a volatile trailing user message

### Depends on
None

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l1-cache-anchor-flag

### Title
feat(providers): add mutableLatestUserMessage cache-anchor option

- `assistant/src/providers/anthropic/client.ts`
- `assistant/src/__tests__/anthropic-provider.test.ts`

   `mutableLatestUserMessage?: boolean` with a docstring: "When true, the most
   recent user message's content varies across otherwise-identical turns (e.g. a
   per-turn memory block was injected into it). The provider places the primary
   long-TTL cache breakpoint on the most recent *stable* user message instead of
   the volatile latest one, so the cached prefix stays reusable across turns.
   Default false — existing behavior."
2. In `anthropic/client.ts`, read it next to the existing `disableTurnStartCache`
   / `cacheTtl` reads (~line 827): `const mutableLatestUserMessage = (config as

   the first request of a turn (`turnStartIdx === msgs.length - 1`), do NOT apply
   the long-TTL breakpoint to `turnStartIdx` (it is volatile); the existing

4. Leave `disableTurnStartCache` semantics intact and independent — do not

✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `4f063cb1`

**Value:** `vellum://` deep links now actually work end-to-end on macOS: cold-start launch opens the window and routes to the right place; hot-path links navigate while the app is running; a click on `/assistant/settings` won't silently drop an inbound `vellum://send`.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

## Architecture

Split-hook design is exactly right:

- `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` → mounted at `RootLayout` (confirmed in `root-layout.tsx`). Route-stable. Handles navigation + window activation for every authenticated route.
- `useDeepLinkConsumer` → mounted at `ChatPage`. Reads from `usePendingDeepLinkStore` (the narrow-waist hand-off) and pre-fills the composer. Only the chat domain knows about `setInput`; store is how the two halves coordinate across mount timing.

**Codex P1 ("Keep the deep-link consumer mounted outside ChatPage")** is a false positive. Codex saw `useDeepLinkConsumer` in `ChatPage` and missed that `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` is already at `RootLayout` doing exactly that job. The split is the architecture.

## deep-links.ts (macOS main)

`subscriberCount → Set<WebContents>`: correct fix. A React effect cleanup that fires before JS context teardown was the only thing preventing `subscriberCount` from leaking — under window-close the renderer process dies before `useEffect` cleanups run, so the counter could stay positive with zero real recipients. Tracking by `WebContents` + auto-deregistering on `destroyed` closes this properly.

`app.isReady()` gate: needed for the cold-start path where `open-url` fires before the app is fully up. Commit title + docs are clear about the timing. Addresses the prior Codex P1.

`ensureVisible as ensureMainWindowVisible` imported from `./main-window` in the main process — correct. The main process handles window activation directly on cold-start without going through the renderer.

## pending-deep-link-store.ts

One-shot semantics, last-write-wins on double-link. Transient (not persisted). All three choices are documented and reasonable. The "two links arriving before consumption" scenario is acknowledged and low-priority.

## runtime/main-window.ts

Clean wrapper: no-ops off Electron, delegates through `window.vellum?.mainWindow.ensureVisible()`. Same shape as `dock.ts` / `app-info.ts` — consistent.

## preload/index.ts

`mainWindow.ensureVisible` added to the bridge. Types updated in `is-electron.ts`. Wired through `ipcMain.handle("vellum:mainWindow:ensureVisible")` in `main-window.ts`. Full chain is solid.

## Tests

- `deep-links.test.ts`: WebContents stub with `fireDestroyed()` — tests the auto-cleanup path. `appIsReady` flag tests the readiness gate. Good coverage.
- `use-deep-link-consumer.test.tsx`: Covers pending-consume, non-empty-composer-drops, whitespace-counts-as-empty.
- `use-global-deep-link-consumer.test.tsx`: Covers send/openThread/unknown event types, window activation call, store parking.
- `main-window.test.ts`: IPC handler registration + routing verified.

## Codex P2 ("Move deep-link window activation out of renderer")

Partially addressed — main process now calls `ensureMainWindowVisible` directly via the `./main-window` import for the cold-start path. The P2 concern about a backgrounded app with closed window is handled: main-process `handleDeepLink` can activate the window without needing a renderer subscriber. The renderer path is defense-in-depth for the hot case. Not blocking.

</details>

*Vellum Constitution — Yours: the assistant responds when you call it — a deep link that silently drops because the user happened to be on settings is the assistant not showing up.*

## Both findings addressed in `83f549e899`

### Codex P1 (consumer only mounted on ChatPage) — closed

Real bug. `vellum://thread/<id>` clicks did nothing on every non-chat route. Fix is the architectural split:

- **`apps/web/src/hooks/use-global-deep-link-consumer.ts`** (new) — mounted at `RootLayout`, alive on every authenticated assistant route. Handles `deeplink.openThread` (navigate to conversation), `deeplink.send` (navigate to `/assistant` + park message in store), `deeplink.unknown` (Sentry breadcrumb). Always fires `ensureMainWindowVisible()` for the navigating handlers.
- **`apps/web/src/stores/pending-deep-link-store.ts`** (new) — Zustand one-shot inbox. Global consumer writes, chat-domain consumer reads-and-clears. Narrow-waist hand-off so the composer pre-fill (which needs `setInput`) stays chat-domain-local without lifting all composer state up.
- **`apps/web/src/domains/chat/hooks/use-deep-link-consumer.ts`** (refactored) — reads `pendingComposerMessage` via the Zustand atomic selector and applies the empty-composer-only policy. No longer subscribes to the bus directly.

Why the hand-off store: the alternative (mount the whole consumer at `RootLayout` and push `setInput` up via outlet context or another Zustand store) would have meant lifting all composer state out of `useDraftInput` — bigger surface than the one-shot store, and `useDraftInput` is intentionally local to its conversation-switch + draft-persistence lifecycle.

### Devin BUG_0001 (docstring inconsistency) — moot post-refactor

Devin flagged the old `useDeepLinkConsumer`'s docstring claiming "all three handlers fire `ensureMainWindowVisible`" but `deeplink.unknown` didn't. The chat-domain hook no longer handles bus events at all post-refactor, and the new global consumer's docstring lists each handler's behavior precisely.

### Tests

9 cases total across the two hooks:
- Global: send navigates + parks + window; openThread navigates + window; unknown breadcrumb-only; unmount unsubscribes.
- Chat-domain: empty-composer pre-fill on pending; non-empty preserves typing + breadcrumb + clears store; whitespace-only empty; no-op when nothing pending; late arrival fires on Zustand re-render.

All green.

Codex P2 (renderer-only activation doesn't help when no renderer exists) addressed in d84b5ef9ab.

The macOS path Codex traced is exact: app alive after main window closes (`window-all-closed` doesn't quit on Darwin), no renderer subscribed, deep link arrives → buffered + broadcast (to zero windows) → never delivered because the renderer-side `ensureMainWindowVisible()` was the only thing that would have recreated the window.

Fix: `handleDeepLink` in main calls `ensureVisible()` from `./main-window` for actionable kinds (`send`, `openThread`), independent of whether a renderer is alive. The renderer then mounts, drains the buffered link, and acts on it. The renderer-side `ensureMainWindowVisible()` stays as defense-in-depth — no-op when the window is already visible.

`unknown` kinds explicitly skip activation: an attacker who could induce the OS to route a `javascript:` URL shouldn't get a UI side effect from us bringing the window forward.

4 new tests pin the behavior:
- `send` + `openThread` each activate the window.
- `unknown` / foreign schemes / malformed URLs do NOT activate.
- The buffer-then-activate sequence (the primary fix path): link is parked AND window recreates so the renderer-on-mount drain delivers it.

Two new Codex P1s both addressed in 4f063cb1f2:

**Defer activation until `app.isReady()`** — cold-launch `vellum://` URL fires `open-url` BEFORE `whenReady`. **Value:** Second use of the push-signal bridge pattern from #32651, extended with the new "signals can arrive before the renderer exists" sub-pattern (subscribe-then-drain + main-side buffering). The convention proves out on its first reuse — and the pre-mount buffering layer is exactly the right place to land it, since deep links are the canonical case where the OS hands you a signal before your UI exists.

**What this does:**

- Main: `parseVellumUrl` (pure, exhaustive over send/openThread/unknown), `extractDeepLinkFromArgv` (Windows/Linux second-instance), `installDeepLinks` wires both schemes + `will-finish-launching → open-url` (the launching-URL trap) + `second-instance` + `vellum:deepLinks:drain` IPC + new `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` IPC channels.
- Bridge: `window.vellum.deepLinks.drain()` + `onLink(cb)` with subscribe/unsubscribe IPC sent inside the callback lifecycle.
- Renderer: `subscribeToDeepLinks` + `drainPendingDeepLinks` runtime wrappers (no-op off Electron), three new `BusEventMap` entries (`deeplink.send` / `deeplink.openThread` / `deeplink.unknown`), `use-event-bus-init` subscribes first then drains.
- Docs: `ELECTRON.md` gains the "signals before renderer exists" sub-section; `EVENT_BUS.md` event table extended.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

### Codex P2 (live-link replay on renderer reload) — closed at `fbdc7bef51`, refined at `bf959ca7ae`

The original `drained: boolean` flag closed the replay case but introduced the logout-relogin gap that your audit caught. The pivot to **subscriber-counted buffering** is the right shape — it stops conflating "has drained" with "is subscribed now":

```ts
if (subscriberCount === 0) pending.push(link);
broadcast(link);
```

This closes both cases by construction:
- **Renderer reload, subscriber present:** count > 0 → broadcast-only → drain returns nothing the second time.
- **Logout, no subscriber:** count === 0 → buffered → next renderer drains it.

Test coverage matches the intent: "with a subscriber present, live links broadcast but do NOT enter the buffer (no replay on renderer reload)" + "logout-relogin: link arriving while unsubscribed lands in the buffer for the next subscriber" + the clamp-to-zero accounting test. The pairing of test names to failure modes is exemplary — anyone reading the test list sees the model.

### Residual race — documented + accepted

The inline comment on `subscriberCount` calls out the sub-microsecond window between renderer's `ipcRenderer.on` and main's processing of the `subscribe` IPC. Acknowledging it inline is the right call — it's not realistically triggerable by user action (deep links arrive on user click, not at IPC-roundtrip frequency), but the comment prevents the next reader from "fixing" it with a more complex design.

### Subscribe-then-drain ordering

`use-event-bus-init.ts:lines ~150–165` does the subscribe-first, drain-second sequence. Verified the comment explanation matches the implementation — the inline note about "any in-flight link is delivered via `onLink` and the drained buffer carries the pre-renderer-ready backlog" is correct as long as the main-side buffer is subscriber-counted (which it is at HEAD).

### Pattern extension — `ELECTRON.md`

The new sub-section codifies the rule: bridges where the signal can arrive pre-mount need both a `subscribe<X>` (live) and a `drainPending<X>` (backlog) surface, and consumers must subscribe-then-drain. This is the kind of documentation that prevents the next contributor from rediscovering the race by hand. High-leverage.

### Observations (non-blocking)

1. **Renderer crash / freeze leaks subscriberCount.** If a `webContents` crashes without the preload cleanup running (which is the cleanup path for `subscribe → unsubscribe` IPC), the count stays incremented. Subsequent links arrive with count > 0 → broadcast-only → lost (no live consumer to receive them). A more robust shape: track `subscribers: Set<WebContents>` on

## Audit-found bug + fix — `drained` flag was wrong shape

Pushed `bf959ca7ae`. The previous "drained-once means live-only-mode-forever" approach addressed the Codex P2 replay case but introduced a new bug: links arriving while NO renderer is subscribed (logout, between hard navigates) would be neither buffered nor delivered.

**Trace of the bug:**
1. User logged out, clicks `vellum://send?message=hello` → buffered. ✓
2. User logs in → drain returns it. `drained = true` forever. ✓
3. User logs out → renderer unmounts.
4. User clicks `vellum://thread/abc` → broadcast hits zero listeners, `drained === true` so no buffer → **link lost**.
5. User logs back in → drain returns `[]`. Thread never opens.

The flag conflated "has ever drained" with "is subscribed right now."

**Fix: explicit subscriber tracking via two new IPC channels.**

- `vellum:deepLinks:subscribe` — preload sends on `onLink` registration. Main increments `subscriberCount`.
- `vellum:deepLinks:unsubscribe` — preload sends on cleanup. Main decrements (clamped to 0).

`handleDeepLink` buffers iff `subscriberCount === 0`. `drain` always returns + clears; no more permanent flag.

This closes:
- **Codex P2** (live-link replay on renderer reload) — still closed because live links with a subscriber present don't enter the buffer.
- **Logout-relogin lost-link case** — newly closed because the buffer fills again when the subscriber count drops to 0.

Residual race documented inline: a link arriving in the sub-microsecond window between renderer's `ipcRenderer.on` registration and main's processing of the subscribe IPC could be double-delivered. Not realistically triggerable.

26/26 deep-links tests + 34/34 bus-init tests green at HEAD.

## Audit checklist — other items reviewed

- **Location**, **abstraction shape**, **DRY** (bridge-type duplication is the documented convention): clean.
- **`use-event-bus-init.ts` approaching ~290 lines.** Each new signal source has grown Effect 1. Worth a "split each source into its own publish helper" refactor — **not in this PR** to keep it focused. Flagging here so the next contributor knows the limit is approaching.
- **No internal-tracker refs**, **no barrel files**, **tests colocated**, **no cross-domain imports**, **file size under 300**: clean.
- **Documentation**: ELECTRON.md gained the "signals before renderer exists" sub-section; EVENT_BUS.md table extended with the three `deeplink.*` rows.

✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `25a2dcbd4e`

**Value:** Closes the architectural finish line #32641's PR description pointed at. The action-registry pattern, NOOP defaults, render-time capture race, and selector-flip race — all four Codex P1s from #32641 dissolve because the state machine no longer lives inside React's render-and-effect timing. Plus: the machine is now directly testable without `renderHook`.

**What this does:**

- New `lifecycle-service.ts` (642 lines) — module-level singleton class owning state machine, watchdog, retry budgets, generation counter, gateway-auth short-circuit, cache seeding, onboarding-redirect coordination.
- `use-lifecycle.ts` shrinks 676 → 99 lines — pure wiring: pull React signals + push via `setInputs`, hand poll results via `applyServerResult`. No state, no callbacks.
- `lifecycle-store.ts` shrinks 110 → 39 lines — `assistantState` only. The store is now strictly an observability surface; only the service writes.
- Consumer call shape simplifies: `useAssistantLifecycleStore.getState().checkAssistant()` → `lifecycleService.checkAssistant()` across `chat-page`, `hatching-screen`, `pre-chat-flow`, `use-event-bus-init`.
- New direct unit tests in `lifecycle-service.test.ts` exercise server-state projection (active + self-hosted), the auto-hatch cascade (nonprod / retired / vanilla-managed branches), the logout reset, and the gateway-auth short-circuit. No `renderHook`, no React tree.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

### Codex P1 (watchdog reset on every poll) — closed at `4a9aade767`

The original `transition()` cleared+re-armed the watchdog on every call, so back-to-back `initializing → initializing` poll results reset the 5-minute clock indefinitely and `recoverStuckInitializingAssistant()` could never fire on a genuinely stuck hatch. Fix is edge-triggered:

```ts
if (next.kind !== "initializing") {
  if (this.initializingTimeout) clearTimeout(...);
} else if (prevKind !== "initializing") {
  this.armInitializingWatchdog();
}
```

A repeat `initializing → initializing` is a no-op kind-wise — no clear, no re-arm. `hatchAndCheck()` calls `armInitializingWatchdog()` explicitly so a fresh hatch attempt still resets the clock. The inline comment spells out the invariant — high-leverage for the next maintainer.

### Codex P2 (pre-mount lifecycle call → null queryClient) — closed at `26521f2162`

`ready: boolean` ships false, `setInputs()` is the only flip-to-true. Every public action (`checkAssistant`, `respondToInputs`, `applyServerResult`) early-returns `if (!this.ready)`. So a child route whose `useEffect` commits before `RootLayout`'s `setInputs` lands — the parent/child effect commit-order race — becomes a silent no-op instead of TypeError-on-`null.fetchQuery` followed by a spurious `network-error` state being published.

This is the structural equivalent of the `NOOP_CHECK` defaults the previous version shipped — same invariant, but the guard lives once on the class instead of being scattered across three action fields with NOOP fallbacks the store had to expose. The docstring on `ready` explicitly cites the race; future maintainers see why it's there.

### Test architecture

Bun's `mock.module` at module scope + `lifecycleService.__resetForTesting()` in `beforeEach/afterEach` is the right pattern for a module-level singleton. The comment in `beforeEach` about why `mockClear` isn't enough (and why every new mock needs a fresh baseline) is doing real work — the kind of subtle leak that costs 30 minutes of debugging a flaky test.

The fact that auto-hatch cascade, retry-budget exhaustion, and the gateway-auth short-circuit are now reachable from a unit test — no `renderHook`, no fake timers, no time-travel reasoning about effect commit order — is the headline benefit of the extraction. The state machine being a class with `__resetForTesting` is the kind of testability boring frontend code rarely gets.

1. **`useEffect` dep array in `use-lifecycle.ts:

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
✦ **Re-APPROVE** — reviewed at `c9a8b15da0`

Two commits since the prior APPROVE at `25a2dcbd4e`, both targeted at observations from that review.

**Test coverage extension (`c9a8b15da0`, closing LUM-2067):**

12 direct unit tests now, +2 from the prior pass — both exercising the recovery code that was the last meaningful uncovered area in the service:

1. **Watchdog → retire → re-hatch end-to-end.** The watchdog is reachable from a test only because `transition()`'s edge-trigger fix (`4a9aade767`) stopped `initializing → initializing` poll repeats from indefinitely resetting the clock. The test captures that explicitly: a `getAssistant → initializing` projection arms the watchdog, the watchdog fires after `TEST_INITIALIZING_TIMEOUT_MS` (30ms), `retireAssistantById` is called with the captured `initializingAssistantId`, then `hatchAssistant` follows up. The structural fix made the test possible — which is exactly the right shape.

2. **`MAX_INITIALIZING_RECOVERIES` budget.** Drives four watchdog cycles where each recovery's re-hatch returns initializing (the assistant stays stuck). After the budget exhausts, the next firing transitions to `buildInitializingTimeoutError`. The kind of off-by-one that would surface as users *permanently stuck* on the initializing screen — now a regression test catches it.

**The mocking pattern is the right call.** `mock.module("@/assistant/lifecycle", ...)` overrides only `INITIALIZING_TIMEOUT_MS`, preserving the real `resolveAssistantLifecycleState` / `buildInitializingTimeoutError` / `shouldRecoverFromHatchFailure` helpers. The watchdog runs in real time against the shrunk timeout — no fake-timer machinery, no time-travel reasoning about effect commit order. Same testability headline as the original extraction, extended.

**Integration boundary articulated.** The commit message names the two branches deliberately left to integration coverage — "force-refresh found active" (recovery branch when `initializingAssistantId` was null at watchdog time) and post-hatch active landing — because both depend on the React-tree polling loop firing `applyServerResult` from the next `useAssistantQuery` data tick. The state machine alone can't reach those outcomes without a poll driver, so `onboarding-lifecycle-sync.test.tsx` carries them. That's a principled unit-vs-integration boundary, not a coverage gap to apologize for.

**Comment cleanup (`ad191fd7b9`):**

Picks up Observation #3 from the prior review. The old comment carried forward the action-registry / NOOP-defaults / selector-flip rationale that became moot when the state machine moved out of React. New comment states the current invariants: stable identity for prop boundaries, `this` binding preserved on call. Crisp.

**Observation #2 (unused `getLocalGatewayUrl` mock at `lifecycle-service.test.ts:63`)** — still present, still unused. Lowest-stakes of the three; non-blocking. Drop on the next pass or annotate as a future-coverage placeholder.

**Observation #1 (wiring-effect dep stability)** — already verified moot in the prior review: `RootLayout` passes `useNavigate` (stable hook output) and a module-imported `resolveOnboardingRedirect` (program-lifetime constant). The wiring effect doesn't re-fire on renders.

- CI 7/7 green at HEAD
- Codex review at HEAD: "Didn't find any major issues" (the lingering P1/P2 inline anchors are auto-migrated from older commits — both verified structurally closed in the prior review)
- Devin review: 0 potential issues
- 181/181 tests pass per commit message

Codex P1 (power.resume no-ops on live SSE — the central case the PR was supposed to fix) addressed in d9985623b1.

The fix is two handlers sharing the dedup window but with different semantics:

- **`handleAppResume`** (`app.resume`): renderer became visible. Reopen only if no current connection — the connection was either never torn down or just opened.
- **`handlePowerResume`** (`power.resume`, `power.unlock`): system-level resume. Bounce **unconditionally** — teardown + open — because the socket may be half-dead from sleep regardless of renderer visibility.

Shared dedup window: a sleep that ALSO triggered a visibility change doesn't double-bounce; whichever signal arrives first wins.

Two tests added for the central case:
- `power.resume` bounces a LIVE SSE (no preceding `app.hidden`) — the tray-resident case the PR exists to fix.
- `power.unlock` bounces a LIVE SSE — same shape for screen unlock.

## Audit-driven follow-up — one real bug + one doc gap, both addressed in 61099b7c4b

### Real bug: shared dedup window let `app.resume`'s no-op suppress a needed `power.resume` bounce

Trace the tray-resident wake path more carefully than my earlier commit did:

1. System sleeps 5 min. Renderer stays visible (tray-resident / full-screen, no `app.hidden`).
2. On wake, wifi reconnects ~200ms later → `online` event → bus publishes `app.resume(signal: "online")`.
3. `handleAppResume` runs: dedup check passes (first fire), **updates the shared `lastResumeAt`**, calls `checkAssistant`, sees `current` is non-null (we never went hidden), returns without action.
4. ~50ms later `power.resume` reaches `handlePowerResume`.
5. `handlePowerResume` checks `lastResumeAt` — recent — deduped, returns **without bouncing**.
6. Half-dead SSE persists. This is the exact case the PR exists to fix.

**Fix**: split into `lastAppResumeAt` + `lastPowerActionAt`. The two handlers don't observe each other's timestamps; each self-dedups against its own action's recency.

**Tradeoff** (called out in a renamed test): the rare case where the renderer both went hidden AND received a system-power signal on wake now wastes one extra bounce — `app.resume` opens a fresh SSE, `power.resume` immediately bounces it. <100ms, no user-visible regression. Acceptable cost for closing the missed-bounce bug in the much more common tray-resident case.

### Doc gap: `EVENT_BUS.md` event-protocol table didn't include `power.*`

Added all five entries with bus-owned action + the future-ticket note for `power.lock` / `power.active` (no consumer today).

### Tests

- **New**: `app.resume` no-op (current non-null) does NOT suppress a follow-up `power.resume` bounce. The regression case.
- **Updated**: "app.resume then power.resume" — the old assertion documented the (buggy) shared-dedup behavior; the new assertion documents the independent-dedup behavior + the wasted-bounce tradeoff explicitly.

28/28 bus-init tests green.

### Audit checklist coverage

Other items reviewed and clean: file location, runtime-wrapper shape (matches `dock.ts` / `app-info.ts`), IPC channel-per-family discriminator (matches PATTERNS.md), three-file bridge convention (per ELECTRON.md), Zustand integration, no barrel files, no internal-tracker refs. File size on `use-event-bus-init.ts` is approaching the ~300-line threshold but Effect 1 (sources) and Effect 2 (SSE policy) are still coherent — a "sources" / "SSE-policy" split is a separate refactor PR if it ever becomes useful.

Reviewed HEAD `238b1bf1bc`. 7/7 CI green (incl. type check passing after Devin's upstream-merge fixup at `238b1bf1bc`). Clean extraction; factory pattern matches codebase convention; type colocation cleanup is a real win.

**Behavioral preservation verified**
- Watchdog encapsulates timer + per-attempt counters + Sentry telemetry. `arm/clear/resetCounters/recordTraffic/consumeLastAbortCause` is the exact surface the transport needs — no leaky internals.
- Per-attempt `AbortController` retained; watchdog targets the active controller via `arm(controller, attempt)`, so a stall on attempt N doesn't poison attempt N+1.
- `lastAbortCause` set only inside the timer callback (`"watchdog"`); reconnect path reads via `consumeLastAbortCause() ?? "error"`. Single producer, single consumer per attempt, cleared on read — correct.
- Watchdog armed AFTER `onReconnect` resolves (HTTP reconcile is multi-second; arming earlier would charge that against `idleTimeoutMs`). Comment captures the reasoning.
- `finally { watchdog.clear() }` around the for-await loop prevents a near-deadline timer from firing during reconnect backoff and stamping `"watchdog"` on a recoverable error path. The justification comment is the right one.
- `cancel()` clears watchdog + aborts active controller before any `reconnect()` re-entry can fire.
- `resetCounters()` at the start of each `connect()` attempt → `sse_watchdog_fired` reports per-attempt state, not cumulative lifetime state. Correct semantics for the L2/L3 decision.

**`import type` circular handling**
- `stream-watchdog.ts` uses `import type { ChatStreamReconnectCause } from "@/lib/streaming/stream-transport"` — erased at compile time, no runtime cycle. CONVENTIONS.md update documents this as an explicit exception to the no-circular-dependencies rule with the TS docs link. AGENTS.md "Common pitfalls" mirrors it. Right pattern, right docs surface.
- The transitional `stream-transport-types.ts` from commit 1 (`5a56d4fbf8`) was correctly reverted in commit 2 (`0de0c67761`) once the simpler pattern was confirmed. The reverted file shows up in history but not in the merged diff — net zero new files in `lib/streaming/` besides the watchdog itself.

**Type colocation cleanup (the real bonus)**
- `publish-types.ts` deletion is the most honest fix in this PR: 4 zero-consumer type aliases were dead exports, and `isCredentialError` was a *runtime function* misplaced in `types/`. Moved inline to `deploy-store.ts` where the sole consumer lives.

- CONVENTIONS.md row tightened: `types/` is for cross-domain shared types with no clear owning module. Types produced by a module live with the producer; consumers use `import type`. This is the rule that should have prevented `publish-types.ts` ever existing — good to lock it in.

Re-reviewed HEAD `fea1bf0958` (4 commits since my prior APPROVE at `0c3af1b42d`). CI 7/7 green.

**One real Codex P1 worth a one-line fix before merge** — flagging at the top because it's a genuine cold-mount race introduced by `a223a8ddff`, not closed by the subsequent fixes.

---

### Real finding: duplicate `hatchAssistant()` POST on cold onboarding mount

Anchor: `hatching-screen.tsx:120` (the selector subscription) + the hatch effect at L155 with `checkAssistant` in deps L418.

**Trace:**
1. Cold mount of `/assistant/onboarding/hatching`. `RootLayout` calls `useAssistantLifecycle()` which registers callbacks in a **passive** `useEffect` (`use-lifecycle.ts:673-675`).
2. Render 1: `HatchingScreen` reads `useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.checkAssistant()` → captures `NOOP_CHECK` default (registration hasn't committed yet).
3. Commit phase: `HatchingScreen`'s hatch effect runs → `void startHatch()` → cloud path fires `hatchAssistant()` POST.
4. `RootLayout`'s registration effect commits → store updates.
5. Zustand selector subscribers (including `HatchingScreen`) re-render.
6. New `checkAssistant` reference. Effect dep flip → cleanup sets `cancelled = true` (good), new effect re-runs → **second** `startHatch()` → **second** `hatchAssistant()` POST.

The **local** hatch path has `localHatchPromise` module-level dedup (lines 47-49 comment explicitly calls out the HMR/StrictMode case). The **cloud** path has no equivalent guard, so the backend gets two concurrent POSTs from a single user's first launch. This is the highest-traffic onboarding path.

**Suggested fix (single-line):** drop the selector subscription, drop `checkAssistant` from effect deps, and dereference inside `handleHatchReady`:

```ts
// L120 — remove
- const checkAssistant = useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.checkAssistant();

// L201 (inside the setTimeout callback)
- await checkAssistant();
+ await useAssistantLifecycleStore.getState().checkAssistant();

// L418 — drop from deps
```

`handleHatchReady` invokes `checkAssistant` 800ms after the timer fires, by which point registration is guaranteed complete. Reading via `getState()` at the call site is exactly Codex's option (b) — and it's the right one here because the selector subscription is what causes the duplicate-hatch dep flip.

This is the kind of finding worth one more commit before merge. Not blocking architecturally; the structural shape is right.

---

### Other Codex P1s — all closed at HEAD

1. **Selection store logout reset (`selection-store.ts:41`)** — CLOSED in `use-lifecycle.ts:583-590`. Guarded reset on `!isLoggedIn || isLoading` clears `useAssistantSelectionStore` (and `useAssistantLifecycleStore`) to defaults before next session. Codex's REST anchor on `selection-store.ts` is misleading — the reset lives in the lifecycle hook, not the store. Exactly the carry-forward I filed against this PR on the prior pass.

2. **Republish chat-layout context through gate (`active-assistant-gate.tsx:41`)** — CLOSED **structurally** in `54b014fec1` ("Move header slots to Zustand, fix gate-drops-context bug"). Header slots no longer travel via outlet context at all — `useChatLayoutSlotsStore` is the channel. Gated routes register content via store writes from their own effects; the intermediate `<Outlet />` in the gate can't drop what isn't on the outlet. ChatLayout's docstring (`chat-layout.tsx:144`) and AGENTS.md L19 ("Don't ship cross-route state through outlet context") codify the rule.

3. **Hatching screen: subscribe vs render-time getState (Codex P1 on `54b014fec1`)** — CLOSED in `a223a8ddff` ("Subscribe to lifecycle actions instead of capturing them at render"). Line 120 confirms the selector subscription pattern. **But this fix introduced the new race in #1 above.**

### Devin findings

- **ANALYSIS_0001** (`document-viewer-page.tsx:76` — `assistantId` missing from useEffect deps): Devin explicitly acknowledges pre-existing — same behavior held when the read came from `useAssistantContext()`. Out of sco

## Re-review at `c5e431754c` — duplicate-hatch race closed, plus two corrections

The Codex P1 I flagged in the prior review is closed by construction in `c5e431754c`. Confirming + owning two mistakes in my own review.

### The fix

`c5e431754c` swaps the selector subscription for **inline `.getState()` at the call site** in all three consumers (`hatching-screen`, `pre-chat-flow`, `chat-page`), and wraps prop-boundary actions in `useCallback(() => store.getState().X(), [])` to keep prop identity stable. This is exactly the shape that closes the race:

- No identity flip on registration → no effect cleanup-and-restart → no second `hatchAssistant()` POST.
- `chat-page` props (`checkAssistant`, `retryAssistant`, `hatchVersion`) stay referentially stable, so the downstream `useEffect`s consuming them don't churn either.
- The `lifecycle-store.ts` docstring rewrite is the high-leverage part — it codifies *why* neither render-time `.getState()` capture nor `.use.X()` subscription is right for actions registered in a passive effect. That's the rule that prevents the next person from making the same call.

Clean fix.

**1. `active-assistant-gate.tsx` — my observation was wrong.** I wrote that the gate "still threads `AssistantContextValue` via `<Outlet context={activeCtx} />`." It doesn't. The gate is a bare `<Outlet />` with no context, and `useActiveAssistantContext` + `AssistantContextValue` are both deleted in this PR (`grep` returns zero hits). I was reading against pre-PR state. - `chat-page.tsx:1253` (`setTopBarCenter(null)`) ✓

A 170-line "TanStack Query migration checklist" in `STATE_MANAGEMENT.md` would have started rotting the day it shipped — conventions docs and framework-mechanics docs have different update cadences and different audiences, and stuffing both into one means neither stays current. Pointing at `src/assistant/queries.ts` + `use-lifecycle.ts` as the canonical example lets each load-bearing pattern stay alive next to the call site it actually protects, which is how the LUM-1814 review cycle already ended up documenting them. Future migrations (LUM-2013/2037/2038) read code, not a side-channel that someone has to remember exists.

**Verifications**

- All 5 anchor line numbers in the PR body resolve to the right patterns at HEAD: `:141` mutation ref stability comment block lives directly above the `hatchMutateRef`/`retireMutateRef` capture; `:204` the `setQueryData` post-hatch seed comment; `:237` + `:270` the recoverable-failure and network-error `setTimeout`-wrapped backoff blocks; `:436` + `:484` the `staleTime: 0` imperative re-check inside `checkAssistant` and the retire-and-rehatch decision path; `:598` the kind-gated data-watcher effect. The rewrite names the timeless invariant — *once we know where we landed, the user shouldn't be silently re-routed by a late-arriving query result* — which will read correctly to someone who arrives here in 2027.

The prose enumeration in the new "Canonical migration example" subsection names four of the five patterns (mutation ref stability, `staleTime: 0` imperative re-checks, `setQueryData` post-mutation seeding, `setTimeout` retry backoff). The fifth — `useEffect`-on-query-data instead of a `queryCache.subscribe()` cache subscriber — is the one your commit message lists at `:598`, and it's arguably the highest-leverage of the five for the next migration to study (the cache-subscriber approach was an early misstep on #32590, fixed mid-cycle). ## Proactive bug sweep — three real bugs fixed in `ab43bc63d2`

Rebased onto current `main` and ran a deep walkthrough rather than waiting on Codex to find these one at a time. Three real findings, all fixed; four false positives explained at the bottom.

### P0 — Per-window readiness state (module-scope cross-resolution)

`renderReady` / `resolveRenderReady` were module-scope. Two failure modes:

1. **Concurrent create cross-resolution.** A second `createWindow` running before the first's events fired would have the second `armRenderReady()` overwrite the first window's resolver. The first window's `did-finish-load` would then resolve the SECOND window's promise prematurely.
2. **Stale-promise hangs.** The existing-window path returned the module-scope `renderReady` from the previous load. If that load never completed (window destroyed mid-load), the next caller awaited an unresolved promise forever.

Fix: per-window state via `WeakMap<BrowserWindow, ReadyState>`. Each `createWindow` arms a fresh state owned by its window. The existing-window re-show path returns an already-resolved sentinel.

### P0 — Resolve readiness on `closed`

Network failure during load or user quit mid-load → neither event fires → await hangs forever. Now the `closed` handler resolves the pending state so callers unblock. The follow-up `dispatchToMain` sees no main window and no-ops — right semantics.

### P2 — Tray dispatches by reference, not by focus

`dispatchToFocused` picks via `getFocusedWindow()`. After `win.focus()`, the OS doesn't deliver focus synchronously — on macOS with the app potentially backgrounded when the tray is clicked, the dispatch could still land on About or whichever window held focus.

Added `dispatchToMain(command)` in `main-window.ts`: looks up the main window by reference and sends `vellum:command` directly. Tray's New / Current Conversation menu items now call it. The focus-transfer race goes away by construction — we don't ask "who's focused?", we say "send to main." `dispatchToFocused` stays for the application menu, where focused IS the right semantics.

### Tests

- `main-window.test.ts`: destroyed-before-ready awaiter unblocks; `dispatchToMain` sends `vellum:command`, no-ops with no window, no-ops on destroyed window.
- `tray.test.ts`: mocks `./main-window`; conversation-items test asserts both `ensureMainWindow` is awaited AND `dispatchToMain` is called with the right command kinds.
- All 7 test files green.

### False positives investigated and skipped

- **Dock listener "leak"**: when a `BrowserWindow` is destroyed, its EventEmitter goes with it. `show` / `hide` listeners die with the window. Not a leak.
- **Hot-reload double `before-quit`**: dev-only with main-process hot reload, which we don't have. Pattern matches the rest of the package.
- **About-route matcher**: React Router v7 data mode matches by path with most-specific wins. `/assistant/about` is declared as its own top-level route, so the `/assistant` auth middleware doesn't apply to it. Verified.
- **URL composition fragility**: `replace(/\/+$/, "")` + `${base}${path}` is correct for every sensible input including double trailing slashes.

## Audit-driven architectural fix — closes the last two real findings

The bug-hunt found two more real issues; both folded into 8eb44e1570 as one architectural fix rather than two patches.

### Dock-About coupling

`visibleWindowCount()` counted every BrowserWindow, About included. Signed-out + main hidden + user opens About → policy flips to `regular` → dock icon appears. Close About → policy flips back to `accessory`. The dock icon flickered on auxiliary-window lifecycle.

We'd already incrementally patched this twice (added `isDestroyed` filter, then `isVisible` filter). A third filter for "is this main" would be a third band-aid. The deeper issue is the abstraction — the policy is conceptually about *the main window*, not about generic window counts.

**Fix:**

- `computePolicy` becomes `(mainVisible: boolean, signedIn, allowAccessoryMode) → policy`. Boolean, not count. The test matrix simplifies.

**APPROVE** at `8ae2dd0b3b` — Phase 2 of the streaming-infra decentralization arc (Phase 1 was #32598). The first-principles question Boss's superprompt keeps asking — *should this even be in `domains/chat/`?* — applied at the SSE-handler granularity. The monolith was always doing two jobs: dispatching ~22 chat-domain events (messages, tools, surfaces, subagents, queue, compaction) and dispatching 8 cross-domain events that lived there only because the dispatch entry point happened to be there. This PR dissolves the second category into the bus subscribers that own the side effects, with two real bugs surfaced as collateral that wouldn't have been visible without the structural move.

### What landed at HEAD

- **2 new RootLayout-mounted bus subscribers:** `useNotificationIntentSync` (notification banner + guardian filtering + delivery ack), `useDocumentEditorSync` (forwards markdown updates to viewer store).
- **3 existing subscribers expanded:** `useAssistantResourceSync` (+4 events), `useConversationSync` (+ `conversation_title_updated`), `useDiskPressureMonitor` (+ `sse.event` subscription complementing existing poll + `app.resume`).
- **Monolith cleanup:** 8 cross-domain cases → grouped no-op with `// Cross-domain events handled by bus subscribers…` comment that keeps the union exhaustiveness check live. `StreamHandlerContext` drops 3 fields + their ref-stabilization boilerplate in `ChatPage`. `home-handlers.ts` deleted; `metadata-handlers.ts` shrinks 150 → 66.
- **Centralization:** `HOME_STATE_QUERY_KEY_PREFIX` + `homeStateQueryKey()` lifted from `use-home-state-query.ts` module-private → `lib/sync/query-tags.ts`. Monolith also retargets `recordChatDiagnostic` → `recordDiagnostic` from `@/lib/diagnostics` and `ChatEventStream` import from `domains/chat/api/stream` → `lib/streaming/stream-transport` (continuation of #32598).
- **Allowlist:** drops `metadata-handlers.ts`/`metadata-handlers.test.ts → ["conversations"]` — both exceptions dissolved because the cross-domain edges left the chat domain.

### Two real bugs surfaced by the structural move

Both are flagged in the PR body. Both are substantive, not cosmetic.

1. **`relationship_state_updated` was missing `home-state` invalidation in the subscriber.** The monolithic handler invalidated both `HOME_FEED_QUERY_KEY_PREFIX` and `"home-state"` (literal). The existing `useAssistantResourceSync` only invalidated `HOME_FEED_QUERY_KEY_PREFIX`. Removing the monolithic handler without fixing the subscriber would have silently broken relationship-state cache freshness on the home screen. Fixed by adding the second invalidation. New test `invalidates both home-feed and home-state on relationship_state_updated` proves it via call-key collection (not just count). ✅

2. **Notification suppression scoping regression** (Codex P2 at `8ae2dd0b`, fixed in `f2a443b206`). The old `notification_intent` handler ran ChatPage-scoped, so the "suppress if viewing active conversation" check was implicitly route-scoped. Hoisted to `RootLayout`, `activeConversationId` (never cleared on navigation — verified by Devin: no call site passes `null` to `setActiveConversationId`) could cause stale suppression on home/settings/document routes. Fix correctly requires **both** `metadataConversationId === store.activeConversationId` **and** `window.location.pathname.startsWith("/assistant/conversations/")` — the URL guard gates only the in-conversation suppression branch, not the guardian-scoped branch, which is the right asymmetry (guardian-scoped should ack-and-drop regardless of route). JSDoc on the new hook names both parts of the check. ✅

- 19 files read end-to-end. 7/7 CI green.
- New hooks follow `useBusSubscription` contract per EVENT_BUS.md; JSDocs reference it; scope naming with reasons.

What was happening: the click handler unconditionally `preventDefault()`'d the vellum.ai link, then called `openAppWebsite()`. Off Electron, `openAppWebsite()` resolves through `window.vellum?.app.openWebsite()` → `?.` short-circuits to `undefined` → silent no-op. Result: in the standalone web build of `/assistant/about` (which the `FALLBACK` copy and the comments on `app-info.ts` explicitly support — "off-Electron, falls back to a stable default") the visible link did literally nothing.

The fix is the right asymmetry:

payload.body:
✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `5609aef1ba` **Value:** Replaces a brittle logout allowlist (every new key needed manual registration to be cleaned up) with a two-namespace contract — `vellum:` user-scoped, `device:` device-scoped — so any future key auto-clears on logout without touching `session-cleanup.ts`. Eliminates a whole class of "I added a key and forgot to register it" regressions, including the auth-token survival risk that motivated this work. **What this does.** ~30 static keys + 5 dynamic prefix groups renamed to `vellum:*` / `device:*` (device migration already in place). `session-cleanup.ts` rewritten from 81-line allowlist (`APP_KEY_PREFIXES` + `DEVICE_LEVEL_KEYS` set) to 41-line prefix sweep with a transitional legacy-prefix safety net. Migrations are idempotent and run synchronously at import time via the new `run-storage-migrations.ts` side-effect module. 38 new unit tests + Devin's 25/25 Playwright end-to-end run.
Full analysis ### The architectural shift is the right one `session-cleanup.ts` went from "explicit allowlist of prefixes the cleanup is allowed to touch, plus an exception set for device-scoped keys that share the `vellum_` prefix" to "everything starting with `vellum:` is user-scoped, everything starting with `device:` is preserved, third-party keys are ignored." That's the same future-proofing move web.dev recommends and it dissolves the registration-debt problem that the old `APP_KEY_PREFIXES` list created. New keys auto-clear without ceremony. The two-prefix contract is also now self-documenting in every store and helper that touches localStorage. ### Two real bugs caught and substantively fixed in the bot review cycle **Codex P1 + Devin BUG_0001 at `edd1680ed9` — migration timing race.** The first commit ran `runStorageMigrations()` inside `boot()` (async), but ES module evaluation order had already pulled `routes` → `onboarding-middleware` → `prefs` → `onboarding-store`, whose module-level `computeInitialFromLS()` reads from the *new* key names (which don't exist yet for existing users). Result: `tosAccepted`/`aiDataConsent`/`completed` would all read `false` for the entire first page load after upgrade, and `resolveOnboardingRedirect` would bounce platform users back to onboarding even though they'd completed it. Fixed in `2de4bb3` by hoisting both `migrateDeviceSettings()` and `runStorageMigrations()` into a side-effect import (`import "@/utils/run-storage-migrations"`) at the very top of `main.tsx`, before `import { router } from "./routes"`. The header comment in `main.tsx` and the docstring on `run-storage-migrations.ts` both name the constraint explicitly, which is exactly the right thing to do for a load-bearing import order. **Codex P2 at `2de4bb3cea` — legacy-prefix sweep gap on logout.** With migrations potentially failing on QuotaExceededError, the `vellum:`-only logout sweep would leave legacy keys (`gw:token`, `voice:ttsApiKey:*`, `vellum_gemini_key`, etc.) behind — `gw:token` is the auth token, so this would have been a real session-leak. Fixed in `5498f72` with `LEGACY_USER_PREFIXES` covering all eight legacy prefix families plus a `LEGACY_DEVICE_KEYS` set that excludes the legacy `vellum_theme`/`vellum_share_*`/`onboarding.lastUserId` keys from the sweep. The precedence in `isUserScopedKey()` is correct: `vellum:` first, then the device-key exclusion, then the legacy-prefix match — so `vellum_theme` (which matches the `vellum_` legacy prefix) is correctly preserved by the exclusion check before it ever hits the prefix scan. ### Verifications at HEAD - **`migrateKey()` idempotency holds for QuotaExceededError.** Read old → write new only if new is absent → re-read new → remove old only if new persisted. So if `setItem` throws but `removeItem` would have succeeded, the legacy key survives for the next-load retry instead of being silently lost. This is the right shape for partial-failure recovery and Devin's response to the P

Test 2: Migration Timing — 4/4 passed (critical test) Verifies the side-effect import fix for the bug both review bots flagged. **Setup:** Cleared localStorage, set only OLD onboarding keys (`onboarding.completed/tosAccepted/aiDataConsent` = `"true"`), reloaded. | Assertion | Result | |---|---| | All old onboarding keys removed (migration ran) | passed | | New `tosAccepted` + `aiDataConsent` = `"true"` | passed | | `vellum:onboarding:completed` exists (was migrated) | passed | | App on `/assistant` (NOT `/onboarding`) | passed | **Why this proves timing is correct:** If migrations ran AFTER `onboarding-store` initialized (the original bug), the store would read `vellum:onboarding:completed` = `null` → `false`, and the onboarding gate would redirect to `/assistant/onboarding/privacy`. ✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `12b5a9f3`

**Value:** Eliminates subprocess spawning + stdout regex-scraping as the only path to `hatchLocal`/`retireLocal` results — gives the Electron main process a clean in-process API to hatch, retire, and receive the guardian access token directly, without parsing `Hatching local assistant:\s+(.+)` off stdout.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

## lifecycle-reporter.ts

Clean, minimal interface. `progress` / `log` / `warn` / `error` — nothing over-engineered. `consoleLifecycleReporter` is a faithful shim that preserves exact existing terminal output AND the `HATCH_PROGRESS:` stdout contract under `VELLUM_DESKTOP_APP`, so no existing subscriber breaks.

## hatch-local.ts

All `console.log/warn/error` and `emitProgress` calls replaced with `reporter.*`. The `reporter` field in `HatchLocalOptions` defaults to `consoleLifecycleReporter`, so the CLI commands get zero behavioral change. `HatchLocalResult` surfaces exactly what an in-process caller needs: `assistantId`, `runtimeUrl`, `localUrl`, `species`, and `guardianAccessToken?` — the token is the linchpin (currently only recoverable by reading `guardian-token.json` off disk or scraping stdout).

`logHatchNextSteps` call updated to `(message) => reporter.log(message)` — correct.

The `keepAlive` path correctly uses `reporter.log` throughout. No missed `console.*` calls in the happy path or error paths.

## retire-local.ts

Same pattern — `reporter` param with default. `RetireLocalResult` adds `archived`, `archivePath?`, `sharedDataDir?`. All three early-return paths now return structured data. Clean.

## lifecycle-reporter.test.ts

Covers the two meaningful behaviors: (1) `HATCH_PROGRESS:` emission gated on `VELLUM_DESKTOP_APP`, (2) suppression without it. `log/warn/error` routing is verified. `afterEach` properly restores `VELLUM_DESKTOP_APP`. Good.

## Dropped retire-local.test.ts

Legitimate removal — `teleport.test.ts` registers a `mock.module` for `../lib/retire-local.js` that leaks globally and poisons a separate `retire-local.test.ts`. Coverage is preserved: `RetireLocalResult` shape is enforced by tsc, reporter routing is covered by `lifecycle-reporter.test.ts`, and command-level retire/teleport tests cover the command surface.

## Codex P2: startLocalDaemon / startGateway still use console.*

Valid observation, correctly scoped out. Threading the reporter through `lib/local.ts` touches shared infrastructure with multiple callers — doing it speculatively before the first real in-process consumer (Electron adapter) exists would mean plumbing with no real validation target. Right call to defer to the LUM-1997–2000 work.

## package.json exports

`hatch-local`, `retire-local`, `guardian-token`, `lifecycle-reporter` — exactly the surface Electron needs, nothing over-exported.

</details>

*Vellum Constitution — Yours: the assistant's lifecycle operations now belong to the host that runs them, not to a terminal process that has to be scraped.*
